column1: # Sections that state a rule which is written down and tested under a DIFFERENT
# section. A claim, not a measurement — `coverage.py` never infers one, and an
# ack naming a case that does not exist is a lint error. Add a row only after
# reading both sections and confirming the covering case tests THIS section's
# rule rather than a neighbouring one; a wrong ack hides a real gap permanently,
# which is worse than the false gap it removes.
# A section whose own body is empty needs no row: `coverage.py` classifies a
# container as n/a on its own.

column4: The intro states one rule — operators are `public static`, any other visibility is a compile error. s25_1_0004 cites §25 explicitly and tests that visibility rule verbatim.
The intro restates chapter-level facts normative in §28.3 and §28.9, plus the `Task`/`Task<T>` discard rejection, which §17.13 states with worked examples and owns.
Pointer prose. Every substantive claim is homed in §35.1, §35.3 or §19.6.

OUT OF REACH. Every clause classifies a delta between two *versions* of one module's interface. A one-shot bezelc invocation has no surface for it — there is no accept/reject/warn/run a single compile could produce. Same format limit as §2.8.3's staleness clause.
